# ISSUE-25 implementation plan

Upgrade `signal-lost.save` to version 2. Keep Phase 1 progress in its existing fields, add a local Observer profile, and recover valid door slots independently. Bootstrap will use one save session for gameplay and Settings, print one invalid-save notice, and display populated identity fields through `STATUS`.

The approved size is `multi_area` and the execution profile is `detailed`. Estimate 4–8 hours for fixture capture, implementation, focused checks, and independent review, plus the coordinator and browser checks. The work fits the approved 32-hour claim budget.

## What we know

- Saves use one key and a versioned set of required core fields. The only migration adds default preferences in v0 → v1. Unsupported versions and malformed data currently converge on `reset`. [Save schema and loader](../../src/progress/save.ts#L3) · [Migration chain](../../src/progress/save.ts#L53)
- The main entry point discards the load status. The game callback and Settings both call `writeSave`, and confirmed Settings reset calls `resetSave` before reloading. These are the production mutation paths found by searching for the storage key and save exports. [Bootstrap](../../src/main.ts#L22) · [Settings wiring](../../src/main.ts#L68)
- `completeEpisodes` grants completion and assigns the designation when it is null. The ending footer and `STATUS` read it, and the browser journey checks both outputs. [Designation assignment](../../src/puzzle/game.ts#L53) · [STATUS](../../src/main.ts#L58) · [Ending footer](../../src/main.ts#L104) · [Browser assertions](../../tests/e2e/episode.spec.ts#L78)
- The save's fact mapping already covers puzzles, transmissions, archives, sectors, episodes, and flags. Sector entry and artifact opening use content-defined grants, including the two FORGE-related flags. [Fact mapping](../../src/progress/save.ts#L107) · [Sector entry](../../src/app/tools.ts#L113) · [Artifact opening](../../src/app/tools.ts#L188) · [FORGE content](../../content/artifacts/forge.json#L4)
- The opening and the episode ending can both enter the hub. The hub prints its supplied boot lines to the terminal log, and terminal lines use `textContent`. The content pipeline already supports a screen containing a list of lines. [Hub transitions](../../src/main.ts#L93) · [Hub mount](../../src/app/hub.ts#L10) · [Terminal printing](../../src/terminal/terminal.ts#L73) · [Screen schema](../../src/content/schema.ts#L179)

## What we're assuming

- Use `profile: { handle, designation, accessLevel, seed }`. Start handle and access level at `null`, use a nullable string for an assigned access-level label, and trim the handle and cap it at 32 Unicode code points. Check the proposed field shapes and cap at plan review. The approved WorkUnit specifies the fields and their constraints, and the local roadmap leaves these values open. [WorkUnit constraints](WORKUNIT.md#L17) · [Roadmap](../../docs/roadmap.md#L14)
- The planned Phase 2 consumers are local BBS authorship for the fictional handle, returning-Observer identity for the existing designation, a label for the eventual access rules, and repeatable anomalies for the stored seed. Use the stored seed for the existing cosmetic designation generator as well. The roadmap mentions seeded anomalies and terminal doors. The BBS and access consumers are inferred from the WorkUnit, and the reviewer can check them against the parent plan if available. [WorkUnit](WORKUNIT.md#L17) · [Roadmap](../../docs/roadmap.md#L14) · [Seeded generator](../../src/signal/rng.ts#L1)
- Each door slot can hold any JSON value, including `null`, arrays, and primitives. A slot is corrupt when its value cannot round-trip as JSON, such as a nested numeric literal that parses to `Infinity`. The planner confirmed `JSON.parse('1e400')` returns `Infinity`. Step 3 verifies that the installed validator rejects it without losing adjacent slots.

## Open questions

- The approved checkout contains no completed v1 snapshot. Step 1 captures one from the original v1 writer and real episode content. The migration test then checks that the capture exercises every old field.
- Browser behavior is pending the authorized `Browser tests` workflow. Step 5 adds cases to its existing Playwright suite. The planner environment has no browser capability. [Sandbox guidance](../rules/lessons.md) · [Browser workflow](../../.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml#L19)

## Implementation sequence

1. **Capture the v1 fixture at the approved base.** Create `tests/fixtures/save-v1-episode-000.json` using the original `createGame` and `writeSave` with real bundled-source content. Use the capture procedure in [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md#capture-the-v1-fixture). Include a failed attempt, ECHO memory, an archive read, a discovered sector, the optional service puzzle and FORGE facts, and non-default preferences. Preserve the data emitted by the original writer, with formatting applied to the fixture file. Confirm the contents include `completed:episode.000` and the original designation before implementing the migration.
2. **Define the version 2 model and ordered migrations.** In `src/progress/save.ts`, share the existing progress and preference schemas between the v1 compatibility shape and v2. Move `designation` into `profile` during v1 → v2 and preserve the exact nullable value. Keep v0 → v1 adding the same preference defaults, then run v1 → v2. Validate the legacy core before creating its profile. Keep `FACT_FIELDS`, `factsOf` and `addFact` as the sole fact representation. Generate one unsigned 32-bit seed with `crypto.getRandomValues` on each fresh save or successful legacy conversion. Accept an injected seed source for unit tests. Persist a successful migration immediately through the guarded session. A new save is stored on its first progress or preference write. A normal v2 load consumes the seed already stored. Normalize the handle at load and before serialization by trimming, bounding its code points and turning empty text into `null`.
3. **Recover door slots and guard all storage mutations in `src/progress/save.ts`.** Add an empty-by-default `doorState` map alongside the profile. After top-level decode, validate each own entry independently with a recursive JSON-value check that rejects non-finite numbers. Contain any validator exception within that slot and assemble the result from accepted entries. Normalize a missing or malformed map to an empty map. Keep core save validation in place for genuine global corruption. Read the numeric schema version before migration or current-schema parsing. For an integer above v2, return a distinct `unsupported` status and fresh in-memory progress. Return a session from `loadSave` with `data`, `status`, `persist()` and `clear()`. Funnel writes and removal through the same guard. Latch the write lock for the session upon detecting a newer version, including if another tab has stored a newer version before a mutation. Preserve the exact stored bytes and return `false` from blocked operations. Keep the storage interface structural and keep read and write failures non-throwing. Make `writeSave` and `resetSave` internal to this boundary or fold their short bodies into the guarded methods.
4. **Wire the session and player feedback.** In `src/main.ts`, pass the session's persist callback to `createGame` and call it on Settings changes. Apply settings in memory even if storage is locked or a write fails. Reload after successful confirmed removal through the session. Use `data.profile.seed` through the existing `designationSeed` option, and update `completeEpisodes` in `src/puzzle/game.ts` and the ending footer in `src/main.ts` to read/write `data.profile.designation`. Keep assignment timing, formatting and the episode completion behavior. Extend the existing `STATUS` output with `HANDLE` and `ACCESS LEVEL` when set. Preserve its link, observer count, and designation output. Pass plain strings through `terminal.print`. Add `content/screens/save-reset.json` with one line, “Your saved progress could not be loaded and was reset.” In `showHub`, add that line to the first hub's boot output only when the original status was `reset`, consume the pending notice, and persist the replacement at that point. The first hub is where the player can see the notice, and a return from the ending uses the normal boot lines.
5. **Extend regression coverage and run focused checks.** Update the existing save, puzzle and dialogue unit tests and the episode designation assertion for the v2 shape and session API. Extend the browser progress spec using the existing Playwright fixture and episode helper. Verify migration, door recovery, write protection, the notice lifecycle and literal-text profile rendering using the case matrix and commands in [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md).

## HANDOFF

Verify the following boundaries against the source and the approved WorkUnit during implementation and independent review.

Consolidate `writeSave` and `resetSave` behind the session. Keep the existing key, preference defaults and fact exports. |
| [`src/puzzle/game.ts:53`](../../src/puzzle/game.ts#L53) | `completeEpisodes` reads and writes the nested designation. Keep the cosmetic RNG algorithm and the `GameOptions.designationSeed` callback. |

| `content/screens/save-reset.json` | New screen content loaded by the existing screen lookup and validated by the content pipeline. |
| `tests/fixtures/save-v1-episode-000.json` | New legacy fixture emitted by the original save writer before code changes. |

Cover real migration, door isolation, unsupported sessions and the existing round trips and designation behavior. |
| [`tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts:4`](../../tests/e2e/progress.spec.ts#L4) · [`tests/e2e/helpers.ts:4`](../../tests/e2e/helpers.ts#L4) | Reuse the carrier control flow and `completeEpisode`. Add cases for unsupported save preservation, one-shot recovery and populated/unset profile display. |

The `Browser tests` workflow runs `npm run test:e2e` against the production build. [TEST_PLAN.md](TEST_PLAN.md) assigns ownership, applicability and evidence for each check.

The planner checked the save key and call sites with recursive search, verified the screen and terminal text paths in source, and checked that both planned new candidate files are absent in the mounted approved snapshot. The snapshot has no Git metadata for independently identifying its commit.

Reopen this plan if the approved Phase 2 contract requires incompatible profile or door storage shapes, a genuine v1 capture fails the documented legacy schema, or the implementation requires a new UI surface or storage dependency to meet an acceptance criterion.

VERDICT: APPROVED # Plan review: ISSUE-25 (Observer profile and save version 2) I checked PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md against WORKUNIT.md and the current source. REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md only repeats the design and test-plan artifacts. It has no earlier review reports or unmerged lessons. ## Audit table | Item | Result | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | "What we know" claims | Verified | `src/progress/save.ts` has `SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1` and a single v0→v1 migration. Any unsupported or malformed save becomes `reset`. `src/main.ts` calls `const { data } = loadSave(localStorage)` and drops the status. `writeSave` and `resetSave` are used only in `main.ts`. `STATUS` and the ending footer read `data.designation`. `content/screens/` has only `boot.json` and `opening.json`, so `save-reset.json` is new. `tests/fixtures/` does not exist yet. | | Fixture capture script | Verified by reading | Every call matches the real APIs and content. `readContentDir`, `loadContent`, `createGame`, `say` and `grant` exist with those signatures. The answers match the content: pattern `417` (normalized, as in `evaluate.ts`), service code `709`, archive fields, `relay-07` `grantsOnEnter`, and forge `grantsOnOpen`. Puzzle `requires` chains are satisfied in order. The service puzzle needs `completed:episode.000`, and the script reaches that first. `designationSeed: () => 7` keeps the capture deterministic. | | Objective: v2 with profile and isolated door state | Covered | Plan steps 2–3 | | Constraint: logic stays in `src/progress`, no DOM or Three.js | Covered | Pure logic stays in `save.ts`. The only UI change is `STATUS` plus the notice line. | | Constraint: handle trimmed, limited, rendered as text | Covered | 32 code-point cap, normalized at load and before serialization. `terminal.print` uses `textContent`. Test plan checks `Keel` renders literally. | | Constraint: every field has a Phase 2 use, no placeholder currency or statistics | Acceptable | Consumers are stated and flagged as assumptions. `docs/roadmap.md` only mentions seeded anomalies and doors. No placeholder fields are added. | | Constraint: per-door opaque JSON, one bad slot never fails the save | Covered | Per-slot recursive validation with exception containment. The `1e400` case is a good one. | | AC1: real v1 fixture migrates to `migrated` | Covered | Real capture, field-by-field comparison, independent fact set, persisted read-back. | | AC2: v0 migrates through v2 | Covered | v0 input is derived from the real fixture shape. | | AC3: corrupt door slot leaves progress and other slots intact | Covered | Unit test with healthy slots on both sides, plus a malformed-map case. | | AC4: newer version untouched, session does not overwrite | Covered | Version is read before migration or parsing. The lock latches and is re-checked on each write. Tests assert zero `setItem`/`removeItem` calls and identical bytes, and a Playwright case covers it. | | AC5: one plain in-game notice on invalid reset | Covered | Status flows to the first hub, with one content-sourced line. Unit tests cover reset triggers. Playwright covers a single notice and none on re-entry. | | AC6: `STATUS` shows the set handle and access level, existing browser tests pass | Covered | Set and unset cases, markup literal check, and the full `Browser tests` workflow is required. | | Scope and sandbox limits | Acceptable | No new dependencies and no protected paths. Browser checks are correctly deferred to the CI workflow. Focused commands avoid listening ports and Chromium. | | Harness and convention rules | Acceptable | `.ts` extensions, no `enum`. Notice text is in `content/`. The seed comes from `crypto`, not `Math.random` or the clock. | ## Non-blocking notes for the developer 1. **Locked-session Settings reset.** The plan reloads only after a successful removal. If the save is locked (unsupported), the player confirms the reset and nothing visible happens. Decide the behavior and make the AC4 Playwright case assert it explicitly. Either the reset is a silent no-op and the page doesn't reload, or it clears in-memory state only. Keep the stored bytes untouched either way. 2. **`__proto__` and other special door keys.** `JSON.parse` creates `__proto__` as an own property. Build the recovered `doorState` with `Object.create(null)` or `Object.defineProperty`, or a `Map`. Plain assignment would change the prototype. Add one unit case for this. 3. **Invalid v2 profile fields.** The plan says to normalize the handle. Also specify what happens when the stored `handle`, `accessLevel` or `seed` has the wrong type. The sensible choices are to coerce the handle to `null`, or to treat the profile as global corruption (reset with notice). Pick one and test it. 4. **Notice lifecycle.** Persisting the replacement save when the first hub mounts leaves the corrupt bytes in storage until then. This is acceptable. Make sure a gameplay write before then cannot occur, or that it also clears the pending notice. 5. **Browser fixtures.** The existing corrupt-save test uses `addInitScript`, which re-runs on `reload`. The plan already says to initialize storage once per case. Use `page.evaluate` before reload, or guard on an existing key. This matters for the reload assertions in AC4 and AC5. 6. **Access level type.** `accessLevel` is a nullable string label. This is a flagged assumption, and access-level rules are out of scope. Keep the type easy to change before the first consumer lands. 7. **Evidence to record.** Record the capture command's exit status and the base revision. The workspace has no Git metadata, so use a content hash of `save.ts` instead. ## Follow-up suggestions (not required here) - A later WorkUnit can add a UI for setting the handle (BBS). - A later WorkUnit can define the access-level rules and their type. {"version":1,"findings":[]} ## Operator guidance > > Write the first-line verdict and exactly one JSON findings block in REVIEW.md. > For an approval with no findings, use this block: > > {"version":1,"findings":[]} > > For CHANGES_REQUESTED, include each blocker with a stable id such as F1, > blocking:true, disposition:"open", and criterion, trigger, expected, actual, > and check fields. Keep prose notes outside the block.
